purpose: Define each Universal Module as an explicit reusable substrate identity owning a bounded primitive model that domains may compose without duplicating or taking over its semantics.

semantics.identity_rule: Each Universal Module has an explicit stable identity.
semantics.substrate_rule: Universal Modules define reusable business/system primitives rather than domain-specific composition meaning.
semantics.ownership_rule: A Universal Module owns the semantics of the primitives it defines.
semantics.composition_rule: Domains reference Universal Modules; they do not copy them into new ownership.
semantics.version_rule: Additive compatible evolution preserves identity; breaking semantic change requires explicit new identity/version policy.
semantics.instance_rule: Module definition and concrete module instance are separate identities.
semantics.authority_rule: Module presence/installation grants no runtime authority.

invariants.rule: Composition never silently transfers semantic ownership: universal modules own their primitives, domains own their composition semantics, and composed members retain their own identities and contracts.

Containment, relation, dependency, composition and projection edges exist only through explicit typed references; naming, file hierarchy, UI adjacency or shared values never create semantic structure.

references.purpose: Universal Module semantics remain compatible with instance/module lifecycle.
